title: Understanding You through Implicit and Explicit Ratings

cues.en: So how do recommender systems work?
cues.zh: 推薦系統如何運作呢？

cues.en: Well it comes down to understanding you, not just you, but every customer or visitor to a website or maybe even a network of websites that share data with each other.
cues.zh: 關鍵是了解你，而且不只是你，還包括網站的每位顧客或訪客，甚至互相分享資料的一整個網站網路。

cues.en: A recommender system starts with some sort of data about every user that it can use to figure out that user's individual tastes and interests.
cues.zh: 推薦系統先取得關於每位使用者的某種資料，用來了解他的個人品味與興趣。

cues.en: Then it can merge its data about you with the collective behavior of everyone else like you to recommend stuff you might like.
cues.zh: 接著結合你的資料與其他相似使用者的整體行為，推薦你可能喜歡的東西。

cues.en: But where does that data about your unique interest come from?
cues.zh: 但關於你獨特興趣的資料，從哪裡來？

cues.en: One way to understand your users or customers is through explicit feedback.
cues.zh: 了解使用者或顧客的一種方法，是明確回饋。

cues.en: For example, asking users to rate an online course like this one on a scale of one to five stars, or rating content they see with a like or a thumbs up or a thumbs down.
cues.zh: 例如請使用者以一到五星評價這類線上課程，或對看到的內容按讚、給大拇指向上或向下的評價。

cues.en: In these cases you are explicitly asking your users, do you like this thing you're looking at?
cues.zh: 這些情況都是明確詢問使用者：「你喜歡眼前這個東西嗎？」

cues.en: And you use that data to build up a profile of that user's interests.
cues.zh: 然後使用這些資料，建立使用者的興趣輪廓。

cues.en: The problem with explicit ratings or feedback is that it requires extra work from your users.
cues.zh: 明確評分或回饋的問題是，它需要使用者額外付出心力。

cues.en: Not everyone can be bothered to leave a rating on everything they see for you, so this data tends to be very sparse.
cues.zh: 不是每個人都願意為看到的每個東西評分，所以這類資料通常很稀疏。

cues.en: When your data is too sparse it leads to low quality recommendations.
cues.zh: 資料過於稀疏時，就會導致推薦品質不佳。

cues.en: Another problem with explicit ratings is that everyone has different standards, so the meaning of a four star review might be different between two different people.
cues.zh: 明確評分的另一個問題是，每個人的標準不同，因此四星評價對兩個人的意義可能不同。

cues.en: Some people might just be more critical than others.
cues.zh: 有些人可能就是比較挑剔。

cues.en: I have even noticed differences in how people rate my courses between different countries, so there could even be cultural differences in how people rate things.
cues.zh: 我甚至發現，不同國家的人對我的課程評分方式不同，因此評分方式也可能存在文化差異。

cues.en: There are ways to compensate for that though that we'll talk about.
cues.zh: 不過有方法可以補償這個問題，之後會談到。

cues.en: Another way to understand your individual tastes is through your implicit behavior.
cues.zh: 另一種了解個人品味的方法，是透過隱含行為。

cues.en: This is looking at the things you do anyhow and interpreting them as indications of interest or disinterest.
cues.zh: 也就是觀察你本來就會做的事，解讀成感興趣或不感興趣的訊號。

cues.en: For example, if you click on a link on a webpage we could consider that an implicit positive rating for that link and the content it points to.
cues.zh: 例如，點擊網頁上的連結，可以視為對該連結及其指向內容的隱含正面評分。

cues.en: Or if you click on an ad it might tell the ad network that you might find other ads similar to that ad appealing.
cues.zh: 或者，點擊某則廣告，可能會告訴廣告聯播網，你也可能對類似廣告感興趣。

cues.en: Click data is great because there is so much of it so you don't have problems with data sparsity, but clicks aren't always a reliable indication of interest.
cues.zh: 點擊資料的好處是數量很多，因此沒有資料稀疏的問題，但點擊不一定是可靠的興趣指標。

cues.en: People often click on things by accident or they might be lured into clicking on something just because some sexy image is associated with it.
cues.zh: 人們常常不小心點擊，或只是因為搭配了性感圖片，就被吸引去點擊。

cues.en: I've learned the hard way that building recommender systems that use click data alone just end up being -- detection engines.
cues.zh: 我曾吃過苦頭才學到，只使用點擊資料建立推薦系統，最後只會變成某種偵測引擎；原字幕省略了所指的內容。

cues.en: Click data is also highly susceptible to fraud because there are a lot of bots out there on the internet doing nefarious things that can pollute your data.
cues.zh: 點擊資料也很容易受到詐欺影響，因為網路上有很多惡意機器人，會污染資料。

cues.en: Things you purchase are a much better indication of interest because actually opening up your wallet and spending your hard earned money is a sure sign that you're interested in something,
cues.zh: 購買的東西是更好的興趣指標，因為願意打開錢包、花掉辛苦賺來的錢，明確表示你對某件事感興趣，

cues.en: well unless it's a gift, but that's its own problem.
cues.zh: 除非是送禮，不過那又是另一個問題。

cues.en: Using purchases as implicit positive ratings is also great because it's very resistant to fraud.
cues.zh: 把購買行為當成隱含正面評分，也很有用，因為它非常不容易被詐欺操弄。

cues.en: Someone trying to manipulate a recommender system based on purchase behavior will find it to be prohibitively expensive because they'd have to buy a lot of stuff to affect its results.
cues.zh: 想操弄以購買行為為基礎的推薦系統，成本會高到難以負擔，因為必須買很多東西，才能影響結果。

cues.en: A big part of why Amazon's recommendations are so good is because they have so much purchase data to work with and it's such a great signal for someone's interests.
cues.zh: Amazon 推薦之所以這麼好，很大一部分是因為它有大量購買資料，而這是了解個人興趣的絕佳訊號。

cues.en: They don't even need great recommendation algorithms because the data they're working with is so great to begin with.
cues.zh: 它甚至不一定需要很棒的推薦演算法，因為使用的資料本來就非常好。

cues.en: Another implicit source of interest data is things you can assume.
cues.zh: 另一個隱含興趣資料來源，是你消費的內容。

cues.en: For example, YouTube can look at how many minutes you spend watching a video as an indication of how much you liked it.
cues.zh: 例如，YouTube 可以根據你觀看影片的分鐘數，判斷你有多喜歡它。

cues.en: Consumption data doesn't require consumption of your money like purchase data does, but it does require a consumption of your time, so it's also a pretty reliable indicator of interest compared to click data.
cues.zh: 內容消費資料不像購買資料那樣要求花錢，但確實要花時間，因此和點擊資料相比，也是相當可靠的興趣指標。

cues.en: That's why YouTube uses minutes watched heavily in its recommendation algorithms and why YouTubers try as hard as they can to get you to actually watch their entire video all the way through.
cues.zh: 所以 YouTube 的推薦演算法大量使用觀看分鐘數，YouTuber 也會想盡辦法，讓你從頭到尾看完整支影片。

cues.en: So in sum explicit ratings are great if you can convince your users to give them to you and that's what we're dealing with in this course with the movie lens data set we're working with,
cues.zh: 總之，如果能說服使用者提供明確評分，這是很好的資料來源，本課程使用的 MovieLens 資料集就是這一種，

cues.en: explicit movie ratings left by people who rated movies from one to five stars.
cues.zh: 由人們明確給電影一到五星的評分。

cues.en: But implicit data can give you much more data to work with and in the case of purchase data it might even be better data to start with.
cues.zh: 但隱含資料能提供更多資料可用；如果是購買資料，甚至可能是更好的起點。

cues.en: When designing a recommender system it's important to think about what sources of data you have about your user's interest and start from there because as you'll see even the best recommender system
cues.zh: 設計推薦系統時，必須思考有哪些反映使用者興趣的資料來源，從那裡著手。因為你會看到，即使最好的推薦系統，

cues.en: can't produce good results unless it has good data to work with and lots of it.
cues.zh: 如果沒有大量優質資料，也無法產生好的結果。
